# What a mixed-integer centroid identity does not imply

Let r=1+sqrt(3), and let C be the convex hull of the three interval fibers

    K0=K2=[0,1],       K1=[0,r].

This is a full-dimensional convex polygon with integer projection [0,2]; its
integer fibers are exactly the three displayed intervals. The induced mixed
length is M=r+2=3+sqrt(3). Its ordinary mixed-measure centroid has integer
coordinate1, by the equal outer masses. Its continuous coordinate is

    (1/2+r^2/2+1/2)/(r+2)=(r^2+2)/(2r+4)=1.

Thus the centroid is the actual mixed point (1,1), in the interior of the
middle fiber. The closed ambient cap x>=1 contains it and has mixed length
r-1=sqrt(3); the two outer boundary points have zero relevant length. Its
normalized mass is

    sqrt(3)/(3+sqrt(3))=(sqrt(3)-1)/2 <1/2=gamma1.

It is even less than1/e: sqrt(3)<1733/1000 gives the ratio<733/2000,
while e<68/25 gives1/e>25/68>733/2000. The standard elementary bound
e<68/25 follows by summing through1/5! and bounding the remaining tail by
(1/6!)/(1-1/7).

Hence an intrinsic mixed-section centroid lying in S does NOT alone yield
the continuous-dimensional Grunbaum constant gamma_q, or its dimension-free
lower limit1/e. This example does not violate the mixed OC target1/4, and
it does not show that this family arises as a minimizing ambient cap section
in one higher continuous dimension. Such an active-section hypothesis would
be additional information, not a consequence of centroid membership.

Subsequent scope update: Sections 11--12 of
`candidate 4c405e76fb81c248`
now prove a universal one-higher-dimensional minimizing-cap realization
for any full-affine-span mixed section whose centroid is an actual mixed
point, using a positive concave upper roof and a sufficiently long constant
lower extrusion. Thus the minimizing-section realization left unspecified
above is now available. That new theorem still does not assert the source
is globally deepest over the lifted body; its rational example explicitly
is not. No global OC lower bound follows from this realization.
